question: Under the International Health Regulations 2005 (IHR 2005), a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) can only be declared for events involving an infectious disease outbreak.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct! IHR 2005 has a broad scope. A PHEIC may be declared for any extraordinary public health event — chemical spills, radiological incidents, or biological events — that poses a risk to other states through international spread and may require a coordinated international response.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: This is actually false. IHR 2005 applies to any public health event of international concern regardless of origin — including chemical, radiological, and biological events, not just infectious diseases.
